teaching.hint: For a range that crosses the array boundary, what shape do the unchosen positions have?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A wrapping range is the complement of an ordinary interval. Maximizing its sum therefore relates to the minimum ordinary subarray sum.
solution_outline.approach: Compute the total sum, maximum nonempty ordinary subarray sum, and minimum nonempty ordinary subarray sum in one pass using maximum- and minimum-ending sums. If the ordinary maximum is negative, return it; otherwise return the larger of that maximum and total minus minimum.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The two ending states are the largest and smallest sums of nonempty ordinary subarrays ending at the current position; the recorded extrema cover all processed endings.
solution_outline.correctness: Each ending interval either starts here or extends one ending previously, which proves both endpoint recurrences. Every circular range is ordinary or a complement of a middle interval. Excluding a minimum interval that touches an end merely produces an ordinary range already bounded by the ordinary maximum. Excluding the whole array gives zero, which can beat a legal answer only when every element is negative; the guard removes exactly that danger.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Returning zero for an all-negative array illegally chooses an empty subarray.

common_wrong_turns: Returning zero for an all-negative array illegally chooses an empty subarray.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained nonemptiness and one-use-per-position; omitted the canonical false claim about existence of wrapping ranges when the whole array is a minimum.
